title: Example 18-11: Diagramming with Two Separate Arrows

illustrates.quote:
Spatial Diagrams with Arrows and Multiple Shafts
a. Place the appropriate symbol of the arrow above the first letter of the word to which the arrow points. (See UEB, §3.2.)
b. Use line mode to represent the arrow shaft. The line should end above the first letter of the word from which the arrow points. (See UEB, §16.2.3, Horizontal Line Mode.)

blocks.text: Tom, did you submit your article?
Two curved arrows above the sentence, both pointing left to "Tom": one from "you", a second (drawn above the first) from "your". Not modeled: F-189 (no spatial/arrow layout support exists at all).

print.printFeatures: Sentence diagram with two curved arrows drawn above the text, both pointing to "Tom".
